destination.name: Alotau
destination.tagline: A small provincial capital on Milne Bay and the way in to the islands of Papua New Guinea's far south-east.
destination.description: Alotau is the capital of Milne Bay Province, on the northern shore of Milne Bay at the tip of the Papuan Peninsula; it took over from Samarai in 1969. The province has 14,345 km2 of land and 252,990 km2 of sea, with more than 600 islands, and its reefs are described as some of the most biodiverse in the world. In 1942 the invading Japanese army suffered its first land defeat of the Pacific War at Milne Bay, and a memorial park marks the battle site. Fergusson Island, reached only by boat, is geothermal and has a rare bird of paradise.
whyVisit: Remember the Battle of Milne Bay

goodToKnow.title: Open-ocean boat trips
goodToKnow.detail: Most Louisiade visitors arrive by private yacht from Cairns, about four days. Local transport there is by canoe or open longboat, and crossings from Misima to other islands are open ocean with no way to signal distress, so they suit only the extremely adventurous. There is no passenger-only shipping from Alotau and some islands, such as Normanby and Goodenough, have very limited lodging, so arrange boats and beds in advance.

goodToKnow.title: Flights get cancelled
goodToKnow.detail: Air Niugini flies daily from Port Moresby to Gurney Airport, 12 km from town. Small-plane flights to the islands, such as the Trobriands, can be cancelled, so do not leave them until the last minute if you have connections.

goodToKnow.title: Ask before you fish or take
goodToKnow.detail: In the Louisiades almost everything is privately owned, even fish in the lagoon. Get permission before fishing or taking anything, greet with a handshake and ask consent before photographing people.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are Alotau's least rainy months, at about 140 to 190 mm a month; rain falls all year, and May and September are the wettest.

notes: Only two reasons supplied (rank 4 would allow three); not padded.

Best months come from Alotau's own Wikipedia rainfall table (Nov-Mar lowest). The national December-March wet season does not apply here and is not used. No source gives a best-months or diving-season statement; the blurb is a rainfall pattern, not a promise.

'Cruise to the Louisiade Archipelago': the research names no cruise operator; visitors arrive by private yacht or small aircraft to Misima. The reason is used as supplied but the tips say plainly it is open ocean and mostly by yacht. The Louisiade 'Stay safe' section is empty.

Tawali is a member spot but neither Alotau nor Milne Bay Wikivoyage pages mention it, so it is not described here. Wikivoyage also says Alotau's one dive shop had closed for lack of customers; left out as dated, but worth checking before promising diving from town.
No safety warning on the Alotau page; no crime claim made. Crocodile caution not repeated here (given in Madang tip from the same country page); add if wanted.
